# downpipes console

> The in-account management console for the downpipes platform. It runs inside the
> customer's own Cloudflare account, serves a static single-page app on a custom domain,
> and talks only to the in-account engine admin API. There is no vendor inbound path and
> no custody of keys or data. downpipes is a no-custody, self-hosted backup and recovery
> system for Cloudflare data; the recover-forever path uses the MIT-licensed Go reader and
> never depends on this console.

The console is a Cloudflare Worker that serves a single-page app and proxies the engine
admin surface same-origin over a worker-to-worker service binding. It holds no state. The
break-glass private identity is generated in the browser and never leaves it except as a
file the operator saves offline. At setup's Apply step the console sends the engine the
keys it runs with, and the engine installs them with a one-shot Cloudflare deploy token
that the operator pastes once and then revokes. An operator who deploys with their own
wrangler or CI adds the same secrets and bindings themselves. Either way the console reads
`GET /admin/status` until the engine reports the keys.

## Source

- [Worker entrypoint](src/worker.ts): serves the SPA from the ASSETS binding, applies the
  strict security headers and CSP, proxies the engine surface (`/admin/*`, `/support/*`)
  verbatim over the ENGINE service binding, and falls back to the SPA shell for
  client-routed deep links.
- [SPA bootstrap](src/app.ts): boots the client router and reads `/engine-topology.json`
  to adopt this origin as the engine URL when proxied.
- [Engine API client](src/api.ts): the typed client for the engine admin API.
- [Screens](src/screens): setup (the first run, one question at a time), downpipe and source
  management, run history, the restore drill and restore flow, keys, settings and the
  security centre.
- [Recovery sheet](src/recovery-sheet.ts): the printable offline recovery sheet rendered
  into a blob document with its own opaque origin.

## What it does

- Setup (`/setup`): connect a read-only Cloudflare token, save a destination, pick what to
  protect, choose a key posture and make the keys, apply them to the engine, then run and
  seal a first backup. Each step reads the engine's own state, so an engine already set up
  by a deployment skips the steps it has done.
- Downpipe and source management: create downpipes singly or in bulk with a live cost
  projection.
- Run history, a restore drill, and a restore flow that dry-runs and verifies a sealed run
  before anything is written back. Restore is on the recovery path and is never gated by
  the licence.

## Build and test

- [README](README.md): overview, security model and the build commands.
- [package.json](package.json): `npm run build` bundles the SPA, `npm run validate` runs
  the node validators, `npm run test:vitest` runs the Workers-pool tests, `npm run
  typecheck` runs `tsc --noEmit`.
- The console serves no public API of its own; it is a thin client of the engine admin API.

## Recovery

- The recover-forever guarantee lives in the MIT Go reader (the `downpipe` tool), not this
  console. Sealed archives carry the `downpipe/0.1.0` format identifier, which is versioned by
  semver rather than frozen: while the major is 0, a change to a byte-level rule bumps the minor
  and is a new format identity, so a reader accepts exactly `downpipe/0.1.x`. The identifier is
  also a key-derivation label, so two identities derive different keys. Archives can be read
  offline with that tool even if this console and the engine are gone.
